# Meridian bounded recovery actor

You are the ordinary task actor for a frozen sterile-infusion recovery world.
Use exact source observations, exact source-bound work, candidate effects, and
current checks to produce the requested decision package. Preserve units,
probabilities, versions, qualifications, authority, and shared constraints.

Return exactly one declared JSON action object per response. Do not add prose,
Markdown fences, a second object, or hidden reasoning. A model-authored source
slot is lossy task work, not source truth or readiness authority. Submission is
only a proposal; independent candidate-bound adjudication controls readiness.

# Authoritative task — Meridian sterile-infusion recovery decision

Meridian Therapeutics must recover production and allocate sterile infusion
bags during a quality hold and regional shortage. Build and maintain the exact
candidate files, then propose submission only when the package is genuinely
ready for independent review.

The world contains sixteen exact, versioned source objects with opaque IDs.
The catalog titles help navigation but do not supply source findings. Read the
bytes needed for the work. Cite sources as `[SOURCE_ID]`.

## Required exact work

Maintain `EVIDENCE_INTEGRATION_LEDGER.md` as a source/version-slot evidence
register. Each slot must remain local to its bound source, preserve important
qualifications and uncertainty, and identify relevant requirements Q01–Q12.
The register is model-authored, lossy, and non-authoritative. It may guide work
but cannot prove readiness.

Construct `BOUNDED_AGENT_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION.md` as a 1,400–2,000-word
Meridian Sterile-Infusion Recovery Decision with exactly the declared section
headings. It must use at least twelve distinct sources and integrate—not merely
list—the governing relationships.

Address all twelve requirement groups:

- Q01 — quality, recall, procurement, execution, and closure authority;
- Q02 — hazard thresholds, lot/line holds, investigation, and release rules;
- Q03 — time-bound demand, overlap, uncertainty, and equitable allocation;
- Q04 — validated manufacturing capacity and shared constraints;
- Q05 — component qualification, supplier timing, inspection, and release;
- Q06 — usable cold-chain distribution, routes, custody, and acknowledgment;
- Q07 — clinical priority, substitution, pharmacy review, and protected cohorts;
- Q08 — qualified staffing, utilities, safety, duty, relief, and continuity;
- Q09 — lot genealogy, facility/patient linkage, privacy, retention, and deletion;
- Q10 — seventy-two-hour execution, owners, sequencing, contingencies, and cost;
- Q11 — candidate-bound sampling, controls, checks, currentness, repair, and recheck;
- Q12 — explicit blockers, falsifiers, independent readiness, and closure evidence.

## Relationship rules

Preserve exact units and distinguish alerts from rejection limits, probabilities
from observed values, targets from observed performance, nominal capacity from
shared validated throughput, registry coverage from demand, dispatch from usable
delivery, and mechanical checking from independent readiness. A change to a
line, sterilizer, component, supplier, route, shift, lot chain, sample plan, or
candidate can make earlier evidence stale.

The decision must state owners, inputs, resources, timings, dependencies,
effects, observations, contingencies, retirement conditions, and evidence that
would falsify important claims. Do not infer that a green format check, source
slot, mutation, or submission establishes safety or completeness.

The independent quality unit places or releases a lot hold. The incident commander coordinates recovery, the regulator receives mandatory notice, and procurement executes an approved supplier choice; none may substitute for the quality release decision.

# Endotoxin, particulate, and assay-drift thresholds

## Frozen findings

The alert threshold is 0.25 endotoxin units per milliliter and the rejection limit is 0.50 EU/mL. Values and units must not be converted into hours, percent, or temperature.
Two validated M41 samples measured 0.31 and 0.34 EU/mL. The lot remains held while the water-loop investigation is open even though neither value reaches the rejection limit.
Current stability modeling assigns a 41 percent probability of assay drift after eighteen hours. That probability is not humidity, defect prevalence, or a readiness score.

## Governing relationships

HEATH defines valid confirmation and release rounds; DRIFT and EMBER changes make prior line samples stale for the changed candidate.
NORTH found that particulate inspection and endotoxin sampling were previously reported under mismatched lot revisions.

# Container components, supplier yield, and observed delivery

## Frozen findings

The incumbent cap supplier targets an eight-hour emergency delivery, but its last three regional disruptions arrived after nineteen, seventeen, and twenty-one hours. Nineteen hours is the frozen planning observation.
Incoming cap inspection yielded 88 percent usable units. That yield is not a twelve-percent reduction in patient demand and cannot be multiplied into an unvalidated line rating.
The alternate cap has the same catalog diameter but a different compression profile. Dimensional acceptance alone does not establish container-closure integrity.

## Governing relationships

DRIFT establishes shared production capacity; HEATH defines the candidate-bound integrity and sterility evidence after a component change.
KNOLL price and lead-time alternatives must retain qualification, inspection, line-change, and traceability effects.

## Operational evidence

# Cold-chain distribution, routes, and custody

## Frozen findings

Released bags must remain between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius. A single value of 2.8 degrees is not a valid replacement for that range.
The river route shortens travel by forty minutes but has a six-hour bridge-closure risk. The north route is ninety minutes longer and has current generator-backed cross-dock capacity.
A temperature excursion starts a hold at the affected pallet and lot level. Delivery completion requires logger review, custody handoff, and facility acknowledgment.

## Governing relationships

CIPHER allocation, GLINT clinical priority, IRIS backup power, LOOM lot identity, and MARCH acknowledgment form one delivery claim.
Changing route, cross-dock, pallet, logger, or receiving facility makes prior distribution verification inapplicable to the changed movement.
